Human rights as you know them (right to a fair trial, open courts, free speech etc etc) didn't exist until the late 1700's with the birth of the First French Republic and the Bill of Rights of the Americas. Rousseau wrote that Man is born free, with all his free Natural Rights which include the right to kill whomever one doesn't like. The problem with civil rights is that they have been given to you and can just as easily be taken away.

I really love old things. One thing is to have a passion for ruins or antiques or old historical buildings (which I totally do as well), but I get really exciting by pretty much anything old. I love thinking about everything that the object or place might have experienced, all the events and stories that could have happened and been forgotten. For example, there is an old farm house and barn ruin out in the woods near me. Not a pretty ruin mind you, just a collapsed pile of planks overgrown and forgotten. I often take walks there, just picturing what has been. The people who grew up there, worked there, died there. To me, the more potential stories an item or place has experienced, the more valuable it is. Hell, I've even spent hours just sitting on my patio picturing what might have happened in my own back yard. Maybe a dinosaur once walked through here? Or an ancient human might have set up camp here for the night? Maybe a battle happened right here where I'm sitting? I live in Norway, and my area is known for a ton of viking activity, especially battles, so I'm exactly farfetched. No one else I know does this and I drive my SO crazy with my ramblings.
